# 4 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The First Brothers Tortured and Killed

---

**1** When Antiochus realized that their refusal was unshakeable, he ordered the torture instruments brought in.

**2** When the rack and all the other torture equipment had been set up, the tyrant commanded that the spokesman's tongue be cut out, that he be scalped, and that his hands and feet be cut off — while his brothers and their mother watched.

**3** After he had been mutilated in all his limbs, Antiochus commanded that he be brought still breathing to the fire and roasted alive.

**4** As the smell of burning flesh spread everywhere, the brothers together with their mother urged one another on to die nobly, saying:

**5** The Lord God sees everything, and truly he has compassion on us — as Moses declared in his song of testimony when he said: He will have compassion on his servants.

**6** When the first had died in this way, they brought the second brother forward for mockery. After tearing the skin from his head along with his hair, they asked him: Will you eat before your entire body is punished limb by limb?

**7** He answered in his ancestral language: No!

**8** And so he also endured the successive torments.

**9** When the second had also died worthily, the third was brought forward and questioned the same way.

**10** He answered: I will not deny the blessed law of God nor will I betray the nobility of my brothers. I will endure everything.

**11** After he was put on the rack and his arms torn away, he was brought to the wheel while his torturers kept calling: Renounce your impiety and we will spare you!

**12** But he answered: Your wheel is not powerful enough to take away my eternal life. Cut my body if you want — you cannot touch my soul with all your torture devices.

**13** When Antiochus and his attendants saw that this young man could not be persuaded either, they had him brought to the fire alive, commanding his brothers and their mother to watch.

**14** But the mother and the brothers encouraged one another to die for the law, saying to each other in their ancestral language:

**15** The Lord God looks down on us, and truly he has compassion on us — as Moses declared in his song of testimony: He will have compassion on his servants.

**16** And when the first had died, each of the others in turn showed the same courage.

**17** The first, having persevered in his suffering all the way to death, said: I will endure every kind of pain for the sake of the soul that has hope in God.

**18** The second said: Do you not understand, you murderer — that in proportion as you torment us, you are being tormented even more yourself?

**19** The third, when commanded to put out his tongue, immediately stretched it out and fearlessly extended his hands, saying:

**20** I received these from heaven. For the sake of God's laws I am willing to give them up — and from him I hope to receive them back again.

**21** Even the king and his attendants were amazed at the young man's spirit, that he regarded his sufferings as though they were nothing.

**22** When he too had died, the fourth was tortured in the same manner.

**23** When he was near death, he said: It is far better, when you die at God's hand, to have the hope of being raised again by him. For you, there will be no such resurrection.

**24** After this they brought the fifth forward and maltreated him.

**25** He looked at the king and said: You have authority over people, and you do as you please, though you yourself will die. But do not suppose God has abandoned our people.

**26** Just keep going — and you will see how his great power will bring judgment on you and your descendants.
